```{r}
#| label: setup

start_time <- Sys.time()

library(tidyverse) # wrangling and visualization
library(here) # project-root-relative paths
library(brms) # Bayesian regression via Stan

# Shared course palette, the same as on the slides.
col_1 <- "steelblue"
col_2 <- "#E07B39"
col_3 <- "#7B3F9E"
col_4 <- "goldenrod3"
chain_cols <- c(col_1, col_2, col_3, col_4)

set.seed(2026)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Helper functions. You only change their arguments, you never edit them.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Step 4: lines implied by normal priors on the intercept and the slope.
plot_prior_lines <- function(
  alpha_mean,
  alpha_sd,
  beta_mean,
  beta_sd,
  n_lines = 100
) {
  tibble(
    draw = 1:n_lines,
    alpha = rnorm(n_lines, mean = alpha_mean, sd = alpha_sd),
    beta = rnorm(n_lines, mean = beta_mean, sd = beta_sd)
  ) |>
    expand_grid(gov_effectiveness = c(-3, 3)) |>
    mutate(fdi_pct_gdp = alpha + beta * gov_effectiveness) |>
    ggplot(aes(x = gov_effectiveness, y = fdi_pct_gdp, group = draw)) +
    geom_line(colour = col_3, alpha = 0.3) +
    theme_classic() +
    labs(
      x = "Government effectiveness (standardised)",
      y = "FDI inflows (% of GDP)",
      title = "Lines our priors consider possible"
    )
}

# Step 7: median and 90 percent interval, one row per column of draws.
summarise_90 <- function(draws) {
  draws <- as.matrix(draws)
  tibble(
    lower = apply(draws, 2, quantile, probs = 0.05),
    median = apply(draws, 2, median),
    upper = apply(draws, 2, quantile, probs = 0.95)
  )
}

# Step 7: expected values (narrow band) and predicted values (wide band).
plot_expected_predicted <- function(fit, data) {
  grid <- tibble(gov_effectiveness = seq(-3, 3, by = 0.1))
  expected <- summarise_90(posterior_epred(fit, newdata = grid))
  predicted <- summarise_90(posterior_predict(fit, newdata = grid))
  bands <- grid |>
    mutate(
      ep_lower = expected$lower,
      ep_median = expected$median,
      ep_upper = expected$upper,
      pr_lower = predicted$lower,
      pr_upper = predicted$upper
    )
  ggplot(bands, aes(x = gov_effectiveness)) +
    geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = pr_lower, ymax = pr_upper), fill = col_1, alpha = 0.2) +
    geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = ep_lower, ymax = ep_upper), fill = col_2, alpha = 0.5) +
    geom_line(aes(y = ep_median), colour = col_2, linewidth = 1) +
    geom_point(
      data = data,
      aes(y = fdi_pct_gdp),
      colour = col_1,
      alpha = 0.5,
      size = 1.2
    ) +
    theme_classic() +
    labs(
      x = "Government effectiveness (standardised)",
      y = "FDI inflows (% of GDP)",
      title = "Expected values and predicted values, 90 percent"
    )
}

# Final task: posterior mean fitted values and residuals added to the data.
add_residuals <- function(fit, data) {
  data |>
    mutate(
      fitted = fitted(fit)[, "Estimate"],
      residual = residuals(fit)[, "Estimate"]
    )
}

# A1: the data with the posterior mean line.
plot_gm_line <- function(fit, data) {
  coefs <- fixef(fit)[, "Estimate"]
  ggplot(data, aes(x = gov_effectiveness, y = fdi_pct_gdp)) +
    geom_point(colour = col_1, alpha = 0.6, size = 1.6) +
    geom_abline(
      intercept = coefs[1],
      slope = coefs[2],
      colour = col_2,
      linewidth = 1.2
    ) +
    theme_classic() +
    labs(
      x = "Government effectiveness (standardised)",
      y = "FDI inflows (% of GDP)",
      title = "A1: Does a straight line fit?"
    )
}

# A3: residuals against the predictor.
plot_resid_x <- function(fit, data) {
  add_residuals(fit, data) |>
    ggplot(aes(x = gov_effectiveness, y = residual)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
    geom_point(colour = col_1, alpha = 0.6, size = 1.6) +
    theme_classic() +
    labs(
      x = "Government effectiveness (standardised)",
      y = "Residual",
      title = "A3: Is the variance the same everywhere?"
    )
}

# A5: residuals by world region.
plot_resid_group <- function(fit, data) {
  add_residuals(fit, data) |>
    ggplot(aes(x = residual, y = region)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
    geom_boxplot(fill = col_1, alpha = 0.3, outlier.colour = col_1) +
    theme_classic() +
    labs(x = "Residual", y = NULL, title = "A5: Do neighbours share residuals?")
}

# A6: quantile-quantile plot of the residuals.
plot_resid_qq <- function(fit, data) {
  add_residuals(fit, data) |>
    ggplot(aes(sample = residual)) +
    stat_qq(colour = col_1, alpha = 0.6) +
    stat_qq_line(colour = col_2, linewidth = 1) +
    theme_classic() +
    labs(
      x = "Quantiles of a normal distribution",
      y = "Quantiles of the residuals",
      title = "A6: Are the residuals normal?"
    )
}
```

# The setting {#sec-setting}

Governments compete for foreign direct investment (FDI), and many international organisations advise them that good governance attracts it.
In this homework you ask whether that is what the data show.

The file `data/fdi_governance.csv` holds 180 countries, described in @tbl-variables.

| Variable | Description |
|---|---|
| `country_id` | Country identifier, C001 to C180 |
| `region` | World region (World Bank codes, such as EAP for East Asia and Pacific) |
| `gov_effectiveness` | Government effectiveness, standardised to mean 0 and standard deviation 1, higher is better |
| `fdi_pct_gdp` | Net FDI inflows as a percentage of GDP, the outcome |

: The variables in `fdi_governance.csv`. {#tbl-variables}

::: {.callout-important}
**This homework is your first full run of the eight steps, and it is the shape of the exam.**
Each section is one step of the workflow.
Before every piece of code, write down what you expect, then run it and explain what you see.
The data are synthetic, so they describe no real country.
:::

The week 8 slides are all you need.
Use AI tools to check your understanding, not to write your answers.
